subject: Lazy Shell
text: The Lazy Shell items require two key items, the Seed and the Fertilizer.

evidence.quote: To gain access to them, you need two key items: the Seed and the Fertilizer.

subject: Seed
text: After defeating Smilax in Bean Valley, the Shy-Away drops what appears to be a piece of paper; reading it reveals it is the Seed.

evidence.quote: After you defeat Smilax in Bean Valley, the Shy-Away drops what appears to be a piece of paper. If you "read" this paper, you'll find that it is actually the Seed.

subject: Fertilizer
text: After defeating Valentina, return to Nimbus Land, hug the wall on the eastern side of town until you walk out into thin air, and the Shy Away gives you the Fertilizer.

evidence.quote: after you defeat Valentina, return to Nimbus Land. On the eastern (right-hand) side of the town, hug the wall until you walk right out into thin air. You'll find the Shy Away again, who will gladly give you the Fertilizer

subject: Lazy Shell
object: Give Seed and Fertilizer to farmer
text: With the Seed and Fertilizer, take the northeast exit of Rose Town to the single house and hand both to the farmer, who plants them in the giant pot.

evidence.quote: go to Rose Town. There will be an exit to the northeast, which will take you to a section of town with just a single house. Enter the house and speak to the man inside.

subject: Lazy Shell weapon and armor
text: Climbing the vine that sprouts through the farmer's chimney leads to the clouds where two chests contain the Lazy Shell weapon and armor.

evidence.quote: This will cause a large vine to sprout up through his chimney and into the sky. Climb this vine to the top. You'll be in the clouds, where two chests containing the Lazy Shell weapon and armor await you.

subject: Lazy Shell weapon
text: The Lazy Shell weapon is Mario's most powerful weapon, with the same Critical Hit timing as other shell weapons.

evidence.quote: The Lazy Shell weapon is Mario's most powerful weapon, with the same Critical Hit timing as the other shell weapons in the game.

subject: Lazy Shell armor
object: Wearable by anyone; lowers attack, raises defense
text: The Lazy Shell armor can be worn by anyone; it drastically decreases attack power but boosts defense to near-impenetrable levels.

evidence.quote: The Lazy Shell armor can be worn by anyone; it drastically decreases attack power but boosts defense to near-impenetrable levels.

subject: Jinx
text: In Monstro Town, climb the stairs near the Save Block to a door with a "J" sign, enter, and talk to the Koopa Jagger and fight him; afterwards Jinx reveals himself as dojo master and can be challenged.

evidence.quote: In Monstro Town, climb the stairs near the Save Block to a door with a sign hanging outside painted with a "J".

subject: Jagger
text: Jagger is not too difficult; just keep pressure on him.

evidence.quote: Jagger isn't too difficult, just keep pressure on him and you'll have no trouble

subject: Jinx
text: Jinx has average health but his attacks either deal high damage or are essentially one-hit KOs.

evidence.quote: Jinx has an average amount of health compared to most bosses, but the real danger is his attacks, which either deal high damage or are essentially one-hit KOs

subject: Jinx
text: Having the Lazy Shell armor on a healer such as Peach helps a lot if you tackle Jinx right when you reach Monstro Town.

evidence.quote: Having the Lazy Shell armor on a healer character (Peach is a good choice) helps a lot

subject: Jinx
text: Geno Boost helps punch through Jinx's high physical defense, and NT220 notes Jinx is susceptible to Jump attacks.

evidence.quote: Geno's Geno Boost can also help punch through his high physical defense stat. NT220 of the GameFAQs message boards also notes that Jinx is susceptible to Jump attacks.

subject: Jinx
text: Jinx must be defeated three times, gaining more HP and defense each time, before he acknowledges Mario as the true dojo master.

evidence.quote: Once you defeat Jinx three times (he gains more HP and defense each time), he'll acknowledge Mario as the true dojo master.

subject: Jinx Belt
text: The Jinx Belt boosts a character's stats and prevents one-hit KOs.

evidence.quote: Your reward for beating him is the Jinx Belt, which in addition to boosting a character's stats also prevents one-hit KOs.

subject: Jinx dojo sign
text: After beating Jinx, the dojo sign changes from "J" to "M".

evidence.quote: The sign outside the dojo will also change from "J" to "M" in acknowledgment of Mario's fighting prowess.

subject: Culex door
text: The third door from the left in Monstro Town, right before the Item Shop, is sealed tight.

evidence.quote: notice that the third door from the left (the one right before the Item Shop) is sealed tight.

subject: Shiny Stone
text: Buy Fireworks from the guy in the house near the girl sitting by five crates in Moleville, then trade the Fireworks to the girl for a Shiny Stone.

evidence.quote: Buy some Fireworks from the guy in the house near where the little girl is sitting next to five crates. After, go talk to that girl and trade the Fireworks for a Shiny Stone.

subject: Culex door
text: Examining the sealed door in Monstro Town with the Shiny Stone lets you enter; save and prepare before entering.

evidence.quote: The Shiny Stone will react to the door and allow you to enter. Before you do, make sure you save your game and prepare for the fight ahead.

subject: Culex
text: Culex uses only physical attacks and a special move called Shredder, which negates attack and defense boosts such as Geno Boost, and has very high HP.

evidence.quote: Culex himself only uses physical attacks and a special move called Shredder, which negates any boosts to attack and defense, such as Geno's Geno Boost ability. He also has ridiculously high HP

subject: Culex
text: Zelikman strategy: Mario with Lazy Shell weapon and any armor or accessory that prevents insta-KOs, Peach with Lazy Shell armor, Bowser with a Safety Ring in the accessory slot.

evidence.quote:
Mario| Lazy Shell(w), any armor or accessory that prevents insta-KOs  
Peach| Lazy Shell(a) is the most important item here  
Bowser| Safety Ring in the accessory slot

subject: Culex
text: In Strategy One, use Peach as a healer and have Mario and Bowser attack normally; Bowser full-screen attacks can hit the crystals.

evidence.quote: Use Peach as a healer and have Mario and Bowser attack normally. You can use Bowser's full-screen attacks to hit the crystals as well

subject: Culex
text: Strategy Two party: Mario LV25-30 with Lazy Shell weapon, Hero Shirt, Safety Badge; Peach LV27-30 with Frying Pan, Lazy Shell armor, Safety Pin; Bowser LV24-30 with Drill Claw, Heal Shell, Jinx Belt.

evidence.quote:
Mario LV25-30| Lazy Shell(w), Hero Shirt, Safety Badge  
Peach LV27-30| Frying Pan, Lazy Shell(a), Safety Pin  
Bowser LV24-30| Drill Claw, Heal Shell, Jinx Belt

subject: Culex
text: In Strategy Two, use up Rock Candy, then have Peach use the Star Egg, healing her only when she is in the low 50s, and do not revive Mario or Bowser.

evidence.quote: Start by using up any Rock Candy you have, then continue the damage by having Peach use the Star Egg. Only heal her when she gets in the low 50s health-wise. Don't worry about reviving Mario or Bowser once they fall.

subject: Culex
text: Strategy Three: Mario with Lazy Shell weapon, any armor, Troopa Pin or Jinx Belt; Peach with any weapon, Lazy Shell armor, Safety Ring.

evidence.quote:
Mario| Lazy Shell(w), any armor, Troopa Pin OR Jinx Belt  
Peach| any weapon, Lazy Shell(a), Safety Ring

subject: Culex
text: In Strategy Three, keep using the Star Egg and Rock Candies, attack with Mario and Bowser, and use Peach to heal.

evidence.quote: Just keep using the Star Egg and Rock Candies, then whale on Culex with Mario and Bowser while using Peach to heal.

subject: Quartz Charm
text: The Quartz Charm raises attack and defense by 50%, prevents insta-death, and doubles the damage of Rock Candies and the Star Egg.

evidence.quote: he'll give you the Quartz Charm, an accessory that raises attack and defense by 50%, prevents insta-death, and doubles the damage of Rock Candies and the Star Egg.

subject: Culex door
text: Once Culex is defeated, his door disappears from Monstro Town forever.

evidence.quote: once you've defeated Culex, the door behind which he was waiting will disappear from Monstro Town forever.

subject: Link
text: After defeating Bowyer, spend a night at the Rose Town Inn and Link will be sleeping in the next bed; talking to him plays the Zelda found-a-secret chime.

evidence.quote: After defeating Bowyer, return to Rose Town and spend a night at the Inn. When you awaken, Link will be sleeping in the bed next to yours.

subject: Samus Aran
text: After clearing Seaside Town and getting the fifth Star Piece, Samus rests in the guest bedroom of the Mushroom Kingdom Palace across from the vault and says she is resting up for Mother Brain.

evidence.quote: go back to the Mushroom Kingdom, enter the Palace, and find the guest bedroom (it's across the way from the vault, which you should have visited earlier in the game). Samus will be resting here

subject: Samus Aran
text: After clearing the Booster section, look in the basket in Booster's bedroom at the top of Booster's Tower to find a Samus doll.

evidence.quote: return to his bedroom at the very top and look in the basket.

text: In Hinopio's Place inside Barrel Volcano, right before the Czar Dragon, the shelf at the back shows Captain Falcon and Samurai Goroh's F-Zero craft and the Arwing.

evidence.quote: In Hinopio's Place inside Barrel Volcano (right before you fight the Czar Dragon), look on the shelf at the back of the room.

subject: Beetle Mania
object: Buy from toad at Mushroom Kingdom Inn for 500 Coins
text: After rescuing Toadstool from Booster, interrupt the toad on the Inn's first floor enough times and he offers to sell you the game for 500 Coins.

evidence.quote: Interrupt him enough times and he'll say he beat his high score, then offer to sell you the game for 500 Coins.

subject: Beetle Mania
text: BeetleMania can be accessed from the X menu at any time in the overworld.

evidence.quote: It can be accessed from the X menu at any time in the overworld.

subject: Beetle Mania
text: You control a beetle along the bottom of the screen and shoot down turtle shells by firing stars with any of the four buttons (A, B, X, Y); if hit, mash the buttons to recover.

evidence.quote: Your objective is to shoot down the turtle shells by firing stars with any of the four buttons (A, B, X, Y) on the controller. If you get hit, rapidly mash the buttons to recover.

subject: Beetle Mania
text: Destroyed shells create a ring of damage that can start chain reactions, wrecking multiple shells, which is the way to rack up high scores.

evidence.quote: The way to rack up high scores in this game is to use the shrapnel of the shells to your advantage.

subject: Three Musty Fears
object: Sleep at the inn right of the Item Shop in Monstro Town
text: The door right of the Item Shop in Monstro Town is an Inn restoring HP and FP; at night the Three Musty Fears visit and ask you to find three flags.

evidence.quote: The door to the right of the Item Shop in Monstro Town serves as a kind of Inn for resting and restoring HP and FP.

subject: Three Musty Fears flag 1
text: Greaper's Flag is in Rose Town; press A behind the flower-shaped Welcome sign.

evidence.quote: Greaper's Flag: In Rose Town. Press **A** behind the flower-shaped Welcome sign.

subject: Three Musty Fears flag 2
text: Dry Bones's Flag is in Mario's Pad; press A in front of the bed.

evidence.quote: Dry Bones's Flag: In Mario's Pad. Press **A** in front of the bed.

subject: Three Musty Fears flag 3
text: Big Boo's flag is in Yo'ster Isle; press A between the letters O and A in the word GOAL.

evidence.quote: Big Boo: In Yo'ster Isle. Press **A** between the letters O and A in the word **GOAL**.

subject: Ghost Medal
object: Finding all three flags and sleeping again in Monstro Town
text: With all three flags, sleep again in Monstro Town and the Fears equip the Ghost Medal onto Mario.

evidence.quote: Once you have all three flags, return to Monstro Town and sleep again. The Fears will reappear, congratulate you on finding their flags, and equip the Ghost Medal onto Mario.

subject: Ghost Medal
text: The Ghost Medal raises defense while attacking and is worth 800 coins.

evidence.quote: The Ghost Medal raises your defense while attacking; more importantly, it's worth 800 coins

subject: Star Egg
text: The Star Egg can only be found in Grate Guy's Casino, and getting there is a two-step process.

evidence.quote: The Star Egg is one of the most useful items in _Super Mario RPG_ so naturally it can only be found in one place: Grate Guy's Casino. Getting to the Casino is a two-step process.

subject: Bright Card
object: Knife Guy hand guessing game, win 13 times
text: After clearing Marrymore, climb Booster Tower to Knife Guy on a staircase and play his yellow-ball hand guessing game.

evidence.quote: go to Booster Tower after you've cleared Marrymore. Climb the tower until you encounter former boss Knife Guy juggling some multi-colored balls on a staircase.

subject: Bright Card
text: Every win gives an item and raises the win counter; every loss lowers it by one; you must win 13 times to get the Bright Card.

evidence.quote: Every time you win, you'll obtain an item and your win counter goes up; every time you lose, the win counter goes down by one. You have to win the game 13 times in order to receive the Bright Card

subject: Knife Guy
text: If the yellow ball was in front, it ends in Knife Guy's left hand; if in the back, in his right hand.

evidence.quote: If the yellow ball was in the front, it will be in Knife Guy's left hand. If the ball was in the back, it will be in his right hand.

subject: Grate Guy's Casino
object: Top pipe on Bean Valley five-pipe screen
text: With the Bright Card, go to the Bean Valley screen with five pipes and enter the pipe at the top, closest to the Save Block, after the Shy Guy waters the Smilax and you fight it.

evidence.quote: go to Bean Valley and find the screen with five pipes. Enter the pipe at the top, closest to the Save Block.

subject: Grate Guy's Casino
object: Jump three times in far left corner
text: In the pipe area, clear the Gold Chomp, go to the far left corner and jump three times (a chime sounds each jump); on the third a platform appears leading to an exit that unlocks the path to the Casino.

evidence.quote: Clear out the Chomp, then go to the far left corner and jump three times. You'll know you've found the right spot because each time you jump, you will hear a chime. On the third jump, a platform will appear, leading you to an exit.

subject: Look the Other Way
text: In Grate Guy's game Look the Other Way, look in the opposite direction of where Grate Guy looks.

evidence.quote: The goal is to look in the opposite direction of where Grate Guy looks; so if he looks left, you'll want to be looking right, and vice versa.

subject: Star Egg
object: Win Look the Other Way 100 times
text: There is no win/loss counter like with Knife Guy; you simply have to win 100 times to receive the Star Egg.

evidence.quote: there's no win/loss counter like with Knife Guy; you simply have to win 100 times to receive the Star Egg.

subject: Bright Card
text: The Bright Card can be sold to a guy outside the Marrymore chapel: first offer 100 Coins, then 5 Frog Coins, then 10 Frog Coins if refused again.

evidence.quote: once you're done with the Casino, you can sell the Bright Card to a guy outside the Marrymore chapel. You can refuse his first offer of 100 Coins; he'll then offer 5 Frog Coins. Refuse again and the price goes up to 10 Frog Coins.

subject: Bright Card
text: You can buy the Bright Card back for 15 Frog Coins.

evidence.quote: You can buy the Card back for 15 Frog Coins, as well.

subject: Marrymore bellhop
object: Overstay in deluxe suite until bankrupt
text: In Marrymore, buying the deluxe suite covers one night, but you may stay as many nights as you like if you do not go down to the lobby.

evidence.quote: The cost only covers a one- night stay, but you are quite free to stay as many nights as you like, as long as you don't go downstairs to the lobby.

subject: Marrymore bellhop
text: If the owner bankrupts you, you must work as a bellhop in the Hotel until the debt is paid off.

evidence.quote: If he winds up bankrupting you, you'll have to work as a bellhop in the Hotel until you've paid off your debt.

subject: Marrymore bellhop
object: Escort customers and talk for tips
text: As bellhop you take customers who pay for the deluxe suite upstairs and explain everything, then talk to them to see if you get a tip; each customer led up pays for one overstayed night.

evidence.quote: when a customer pays for the deluxe suite, you take them upstairs and explain everything, just like the original bellhop did when you stayed there. Afterwards, talk to the customers and see if you get a tip off of them. Leading one customer up to the suite will pay for one of the extra nights you overstayed in the suite.

subject: Marrymore bellhop
text: When the debt is fully repaid you are released from bellhop duty.

evidence.quote: When the debt is fully repaid, you're finally released into the world again.

subject: Melody Bay
object: Right of Tadpole Pond main screen
text: Melody Bay is off the right side of the main Tadpole Pond screen, a pond set up like musical notation where Toadofsky needs help composing by playing songs.

evidence.quote: Off to the right side of the main screen of Tadpole Pond is an area called Melody Bay.

subject: Melody Bay
object: Mi Re Do Ti La So Fa
text: From left to right the notes are Mi Re Do Ti La So Fa.

evidence.quote: From left to right, the notes are: Mi Re Do Ti La So Fa.

subject: Frogfucius' Suite #18
text: Song 1, Frogfucius' Suite #18, is on a piece of paper behind Frogfucius at Tadpole Pond, available once Rose Town is unlocked; notes So La Mi Re Do Re Do Re.

evidence.quote: 1| Frogfucius' Suite #18| At Tadpole Pond, on a piece of paper behind Frogfucius. Available as soon as you unlock Rose Town.| So La Mi Re Do Re Do Re

subject: Moleville Blues
text: Song 2, Moleville Blues, is learned in Moleville Mountain after the third Star Piece by talking to the miners near the blown-up wall; notes Mi Do So Do Re La Ti Do.

evidence.quote: 2| Moleville Blues| In Moleville Mountain after you've obtained the third Star Piece. Talk to the miners near where you blew up the wall.| Mi Do So Do Re La Ti Do

subject: Star Song
text: Song 3, Star Song, is from the star upstairs in the first house on the left in Monstro Town; notes La Ti Do Re So Do Re Mi.

evidence.quote: 3| Star Song| In Monstro Town, first house on the left. Talk to the star upstairs to hear the song. Available as soon as you reach Monstro Town.| La Ti Do Re So Do Re Mi

subject: Melody Bay
text: After the Star Song, Toadofsky asks you to write a conclusion and you can input any melody.

evidence.quote: After the Star Song, Toadofsky will ask you to write a conclusion to the piece. You can input any melody you like.

subject: Melody cards
text: Playing a song for Toadofsky earns a card that lets you buy items at the Juice Bar in Tadpole Pond, left of the tadpole bridge to Frogfucius.

evidence.quote: After you successfully play a song for Toadofsky, he'll give you a card. These cards will allow you to buy items at the Juice Bar in Tadpole Pond (left of the tadpole bridge to Frogfucius on the mainland).

subject: Alto Card melody
text: Alto card (Frogfucius' Suit #18): Froggie Drink 14 Coins, Elixir 38 Coins.

evidence.quote: Alto| Frogfucius' Suit #18| Froggie Drink (14 Coins), Elixir (38 Coins)

subject: Tenor Card
text: Tenor card (Moleville Blues): Froggie Drink 12 Coins, Elixir 36 Coins, Megalixir 90 Coins.

evidence.quote: Tenor| Moleville Blues| Froggie Drink (12 Coins), Elixir (36 Coins), Megalixir (90 Coins)

subject: Soprano Card
text: Soprano card (Star Song): Froggie Drink 8 Coins, Elixir 24 Coins, Megalixir 60 Coins, KeroKeroCola 200 Coins.

evidence.quote: Soprano| Star Song| Froggie Drink (8 Coins), Elixir (24 Coins), Megalixir (60 Coins), KeroKeroCola (200 Coins
